notes: §1985:IX.4.3.2 prints DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ] [ END-DELETE ], in the sequence §1985:IV.2.1 makes binding ("A general format is the specific arrangement of the elements of a clause or a statement"). deleteStatement with the shared conditionalPhrases loop parses it (RECORD optional), BindDelete binds it, and the later additions are refused at --std 85: NOT INVALID KEY before INVALID KEY by VisitConditionalPhrases through ConditionalPhraseAssociation.OutOfPrintedOrder (COBOL0900, the PB5158 fix; §2002:F.2 item 33 is the 2002 relaxation), RETRY by VisitRetryPhrase and DELETE FILE by VisitDeleteFileStatement (COBOL0900), a second INVALID KEY by Associates (COBOL2269), AT END and a missing file-name by the parser (COBOL0001/COBOL5506). Probes at 85 (work-rs-04/c1): b) order, twice, atend, noop refused; c) retry, delfile refused; e) indexed random and relative dynamic files, RECORD omitted, invalid key 23 runs INVALID KEY only, DELETE after a failed OPEN I-O (35) gives 49 and runs neither phrase; a/d/f do not apply to a file-name operand. The witness deletes a present and an absent key in the printed order. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5158 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-04.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-04-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ]"; 2023: "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ retry-phrase ] ┌ │ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 │ … NOT INVALID KEY … │ ┘ (choice indicators)". Same record format, but 2023 adds an optional retry-phrase. Its choice indicators also allow INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY in either order, so it accepts programs 1985 refuses.
